newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Traffic halts in Palestinian protest.
newsitem.headline: Traffic halts in Palestinian protest.

text.p: Traffic came to a halt in the West Bank and Gaza Strip for five minutes on Wednesday in a show of support for the Palestinian Authority and a protest against Israel's closure of the self-rule areas.
Witnesses across the West Bank and Gaza Strip said Palestinian motorists stopped their vehicles in the streets at noon (1000 GMT) for five minutes. Pedestrians also halted in silence.

Leaders of Palestinian factions and PLO officials called the strike, which was publicised on the Voice of Palestine radio as part of peaceful protests following last week's violence in which 57 Palestinians and 15 Israelis were killed.
Israel imposed tough travel restrictions on Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip folowing the violence, barring Arabs from moving from one area to another.

The strike was also aimed at showing support for Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, who was holding talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Washington on resolving differences over implementation of self-rule deals which call for further Israeli army redeployment in the West Bank.
In the West Bank town of Hebron, Palestinians threw stones at Israeli soldiers as authorities briefly lifted a week-long military curfew to allow residents to restock on food supplies.
Witnesses said the Israeli army re-imposed the curfew quickly after the stone-throwing. There were no reports of injuries.
Other parts of the West Bank and the Gaza Strip remained calm, Palestinians said.
